concerns.recommendation: Disambiguate which physical project this row is: the SCOP EPCF 28-in gas twin (concept/FEED 2017, never built, excluded from the 2024-25 revived crude-only Basra-Haditha project) vs the 2019-approved Basra Oil Company replacement gas line reported near-complete in Jan 2021. Verify whether the latter entered service (possible missing operating pipeline).
concerns.researcher_notes: The row conflates two distinct projects. (A) The 28-in / 258 MMSCFD / 350 km specs and the saymar refs belong to the gas component of SCOP's EPCF strategic pipeline (Rumaila PS1A to Al-Najaf PS3A, twin of the 56-in crude line), whose PDF states status 'FEED & EISHA completed for Pump Stations, and Concept for the Pipeline' — i.e., it never reached construction; the project was rebooted in Aug-Dec 2024 as the $4.6bn Basra-Haditha CRUDE pipeline with no gas component mentioned in either the SCOP ministry clarification (gulfoilandgas, 2024-08-06) or AGBI's cabinet-approval coverage (2024-12-31). (B) The ProposalYear/ConstructionYear=2019 and the route narrative trace to the Independent Arabia article (2021-01-19), which describes a DIFFERENT effort: a new gas pipeline approved by the government in 2019, laid along the route of the old decrepit Rumaila-to-Middle-Euphrates gas line under Basra Oil Company projects directorate, 'nearing completion' of pipe-laying in Jan 2021, to feed Samawa and Najaf power plants and cement works. I found NO 2021-2026 EN/AR news of that line's completion, commissioning, or continued construction (searched: Rumaila/Najaf gas pipeline completion; Arabic for the pipeline, Najaf/Samawa power-plant gas arrival, SCOP progress). A corridor gas pipeline project is real (not a phantom), but as recorded — EPCF specs + 2019 construction dates — the specific entity may not exist as such: the EPCF twin never began construction, and the 2019-21 line, if it is the row's subject, may be operating unnoticed. Duplicate check vs the 16-row Iraq gas roster: no other Rumaila/Najaf row; P7573 Basra-Ceyhan and P7459 Faiha-North Rumaila are distinct. Classification (gas, transmission) is correct for either interpretation.

concerns.recommendation: Discovery candidate + conflation check: a real Iraq->Kuwait gas pipeline from Rumaila (~400 MMcf/d) operated until 1990 and appears untracked in GGIT. Confirm P0481 describes the 2017 proposal only, and assess the historic line as a separate retired entity.
concerns.researcher_notes: The same Al-Ahram/Reuters article records that 'Iraq used to supply Kuwait with gas from Rumaila, around 400 million cubic feet per day, halted shortly after the 1990 invasion'. That is a distinct, physically-built, now-retired pipeline -- different era, different capacity (400 vs 200 MMcf/d) -- and I did not find it as a row in GGIT's Iraq set. Two consequences. (1) Discovery: it may warrant a retired row, subject to the usual 2-independent-source test; a single 2017 news aside is not enough on its own to create an entity. (2) Data hygiene on P0481: because both share the Rumaila origin and the Iraq->Kuwait pair, there is a real risk the row silently blends the historic line with the 2017 Toyo proposal. The 2.06 bcm/y capacity is traceable to the 2017 proposal's 200 MMcf/d, so the row does look like the proposal -- but confirm rather than assume.

concerns.researcher_notes: The sheet's OWN support for this row is two OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletins (ASB 2012 p.75; ASB 2017) — aggregate national-statistics documents that report country-level pipeline totals, NOT a source that names a 'Baiji-K3-Al Kaem gas pipeline' or gives its route/length/diameter/capacity. So the cited source does not corroborate the specific pipeline. Independent searching (EN + AR: Iraqi press, North Gas Company, oil ministry, MEED, EIA, USGS mineral yearbooks, FAS/globalsecurity Al-Qaim files) surfaced NO independent source that names this pipeline or gives any of its specs. Every apparent web 'confirmation' of a 'Baiji-K3-Al Qaim gas pipeline' traces straight back to gem.wiki (circular). The underlying physical premise is partly plausible — the Al-Qa'im fertilizer/phosphate complex (real; FAS: 380 km WNW of Baghdad, 34°22'N 41°07'E; produced ammonia 1984–1990s using natural-gas feedstock) was historically gas-supplied via North Gas Company (Kirkuk associated gas processed and moved via Baiji), so a Baiji→Al-Qa'im gas corridor is physically conceivable. But I could not independently document it as a discrete, named, operating transmission line. Classification note: the name uses OIL-pipeline station nomenclature (K2=Baiji, K3=Haditha pump station) and a 16-inch diameter identical to the crude 'Baiji-Hadithah' (16", 84 mi) and 'Iraq-Jordan' (K3→Tarbil, 16", 219 mi) lines in the GulfPub oil roster — raising the possibility this 'gas' row was constructed from oil-corridor station names. Duplicate check: NOT the same as P2231 'North Gas-Baiji' (→Saladin, 145 km, 24") nor P4401 'Okaz/Akkas' (Anbar, 30 km, 16"); no other roster row runs Baiji→Al-Qa'im, so no in-roster duplicate found. Net: existence is weakly supported at best; sole citation is aggregate and does not name the line.

LOOSE END, do not lose it: P4054's Capacity=94 MMcf/d has no counterpart in either ASB edition and no home in the map source either -- capture it in the merge or lose it deliberately, don't drop it silently. So the merge rests on the shared 18-inch diameter and the shared Trans-Iraq trunk, NOT on the endpoint string, which cannot distinguish the two facilities. The diameter match makes P4066 much the likelier target, but it is not proof; if the Jafar map can be re-read at higher resolution to show which Daura facility the label terminates at, do that first.

concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + DUPLICATE re-audit. The gem.wiki page is a stub: Location and Start Year blank, no endpoints, no route, and its SOLE citation is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' (wiki_citations.json confirms exactly one reference). The OPEC ASB is a country-level statistics compendium and does NOT name individual pipelines, so this row's only support is a generic aggregate that does not name a 'Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha' line. Every web trace of the exact name 'Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha gas pipeline' resolves back to GEM itself; no independent source names this specific 470 km / 42 in / 11.03 bcm/y line. That is a self-referential-support flag. HOWEVER the underlying physical thing is real: independent sources document a 42-inch Iraqi 'national dry gas pipeline' backbone. The Iraqi Economists Network report (Ahmed A. Al-Jibawi, 2025, 'Shedding Light on Recent Oil & Gas Pipeline Projects in Iraq', iraqieconomists.net) repeatedly references 'the 42-inch national dry gas pipeline' as an existing trunk that other lines bifurcate from and feed into (e.g. the Feb-2025 Shatt Al-Basrah 42-inch line joining it; the Gharraf 20-inch line joining 'the 42-inch national dry gas pipeline'; a 42-inch line bifurcating from the national dry gas pipeline at Mahmoodia south of Baghdad). [That PDF is a legitimate independent source but url_verifier cannot read PDF byte streams, so it is cited here in notes rather than in proposed_refs.] Rawabet Center's history of Iraqi gas confirms a 'national network of gas... extends from the south to Baghdad and the center to meet the northern network to Kirkuk', with power stations built at al-Nasiriyah, Hilla and Najaf in the 1980s. So: the 42-inch national dry-gas trunk physically exists and serves the Nasiriyah/central corridor. The problem is that GEM appears to have captured this ONE backbone (plus its feeder branches) as MULTIPLE overlapping rows: P4061 'National Gas Pipeline' (600 km, 42 in) and P1852 'Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha' (470 km, 42 in) are both the 42-inch national dry-gas trunk under two names; and the 'Trans-Iraq(i)' family (P1852 trunk + P4062/P4064/P4065/P4066 short 24/18-in branches to Hilla/Najaf/Dewania/Daura power stations, all also citing OPEC ASB 2012) looks like one harvested table. CLASSIFICATION is fine (dry-gas transmission trunk, correctly Gas, not an oil/NGL line, distinct from the 42-in crude Strategic Pipeline). SPEC caveat: name says 'Nasriyaha' (Nasiriyah, ~180 km from Basra) but LengthKnown=470 km implies the line reaches the Baghdad area, an internal inconsistency; none of 470 km / 42 in / 11.03 bcm/y could be tied to any source that actually names this line, so all specs are unverified against an independent naming source. Not a phantom, but as entered it is a probable duplicate of P4061 with GEM-only, aggregate-cited specs.

concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real. The sheet's only citation (gem.wiki -> ahewar.org aid=757740, an Arabic translation of a Middle East mega-projects listicle; page is windows-1256 encoded) DOES describe this pipeline: Basra gas-gathering Phase 1 will capture/dry gas from compression stations at the West Qurna 1 & 2 fields and move it via a 40-inch, 50-km pipeline to the North Rumaila NGL plant, with an 8-inch condensate line alongside to a slug catcher; project 'suspended a long time, revived 2017, now expected complete in 2025'. Independently, Oil & Gas Journal (2016-03-07, 'Plant, pipeline reconfiguration boosts Iraqi NGL yield') documents the same physical line: 'BGC in 2012 resumed work on a partially completed 40-in. OD low-pressure gas pipeline from the West Qurna field to a new IBC station at the NR NGL plant. By mid-2015 this pipeline was operational and delivering 80 MMcfd of sour gas to the plant from DS-7 and DS-8' - the first-ever gas capture from West Qurna. Basrah Gas Company's own operations page confirms ongoing gathering from Rumaila, West Qurna 1 and Zubair into its NGL plants. CLASSIFICATION (the concern): this is a low-pressure SOUR associated-gas line from field degassing/compression stations (DS-7/DS-8) into an NGL processing plant - the textbook definition of a gathering/feed line, operated by Basrah Gas Company (South Gas Co 51% / Shell 44% / Mitsubishi 5%); GEM has PipelineType=transmission, controlled vocab has 'gathering'. Whether GGIT keeps low-pressure sour feeder lines is a scope call, hence concern rather than silent pass. STATUS/SPEC error exposed: GEM Status=construction + StartYear1=2025 is a misreading of the ahewar listicle - its '2025' completion refers to the overall revived Basra gas programme (FLNG etc.), while the 40-in line itself has been OPERATING since mid-2015 (OGJ); BGC and MEES (2025-10-24) confirm West Qurna-1 gas is being gathered/processed today; searched English + Arabic 2024-2026 and found NO new West Qurna->Rumaila line under construction (the only WQ-2 gas work is the SESM processing-facility contract of Nov 2023, not a pipeline). Staged as a status change in status_reviews. DUPLICATE check vs the 16-row roster: no match - P7459 Faiha-North Rumaila is a separate 20-in line from a different field, P4041 North Rumela-Al-Najaf runs the other direction (28-in), P7436/P7437 are the Artawi BNGL EPSCC lines (incl. the separate 13.7 km NR NGL feed); the 40-in/50-km WQ->NR line appears only once. ATTRIBUTION: Operator/Owner blank in GEM; sources support Basrah Gas Company - suggest staging on the OperatorsOwners tab. FuelSource 'Qurna' should ideally read 'West Qurna'. Length 50 km rests on the single ahewar listicle (OGJ gives no length) - kept, tier low.

concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed and real. The sheet's sole cited source (al-mirbad.com/detail/157543, dated 2 May 2024, a program interview with the project supervisory committee of South Gas Company / شركة غاز الجنوب) is live and directly on-point. It states the raw feed gas ('الغاز المغذي الخام') to the Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas investment project arrives via two pipes: pipe #1 = 20-inch, 120 MMcf/d from Gharraf field; pipe #2 = 14-inch, 80 MMcf/d from the Nasiriyah field ('الأنبوب الثاني من 14 ... بطاقة 80 مقمق من حقل الناصرية'). P7445 is that second (Nasiriyah) feeder. Existence is independently corroborated: Egypt Oil & Gas ('Iraq's Nasiriyah, Gharraf Gas Fields Project Nears Operational Phase') and Baker Hughes ('SGC awards BHGE contract for recovery of flare gas for Nassiriya and Al Gharraf oilfields') both confirm the same project (~200 MMcf/d combined processing, South Gas Company operator, Baker Hughes/CPECC as contractors, Q1-2027 startup). Not GEM-only. CLASSIFICATION (the concern): al-mirbad explicitly describes P7445 as a raw-feed-gas intake pipe delivering wet associated gas from the wellfield to a processing plant that then produces dry gas / LPG via 'field processing and plant processing' ('معالجة حقلية ومعالجة مصنعية'). That is a gathering/feeder line, not a transmission pipeline; GEM's PipelineType='transmission' is misclassified. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any roster PID -- the companion 20-in/120-MMcf/d Gharraf feeder from the same project is NOT in the roster, so P7445 is the sole GEM entry for the Nasiriyah leg. ATTRIBUTION confirmed: operator South Gas Company and owner Iraq Ministry of Oil (SGC is the Ministry's southern gas arm) match al-mirbad + Baker Hughes; FuelSource 'Nasiriyah Field' and StartState/Province 'Dhi Qar' (Nasiriyah is the Dhi Qar capital) both correct. concerns.recommendation: REMOVE FROM GGIT and refer to GOIT as a refined-products line. This is a GAS OIL (diesel) export pipeline, not a natural-gas pipeline. Do not merely re-label Fuel -- GGIT tracks gas transmission, so the row does not belong in this tracker at all. Preserve the specs (46 km, 8-10in, Shouibah PS -> Khor al-Zubair port, Oil Projects Co, rehabilitated July 2024) in the GOIT referral.
concerns.researcher_notes:
The row's own source proves the misclassification. al-Mirbad, 19 July 2024, headline: 'شركة خطوط الأنابيب النفطية تعلن عن إنجاز تأهيل أنبوب تصدير زيت الغاز (شعيبة - ميناء خور الزبير)'. Body: 'أنجاز أعمال تأهيل أنبوب تصدير زيت الغاز 8 - 10 عقدة، وبمسافة 46 كم' and the purpose 'يهدف إلى زيادة الطاقة التصديرية لوقود زيت الغاز عبر المنفذ الجنوبي' -- to increase the EXPORT capacity of GAS OIL FUEL through the southern outlet.

THE MECHANISM IS A FALSE FRIEND IN TRANSLATION. Arabic 'زيت الغاز' is literally 'gas oil' and means DIESEL / gasoil -- a refined liquid petroleum product. It is not natural gas ('غاز طبيعي') and not 'gas' in the GGIT sense. A word-level reading of 'الغاز' in that phrase produces exactly this error, and everything downstream then looks consistent: the specs match, the operator matches, the date matches. That is what makes this class dangerous -- the row is perfectly sourced and completely misfiled.

CORROBORATING DETAIL, all pointing at liquids: the destination is 'ميناء خور الزبير النفطية' -- the Khor al-Zubair OIL port, an export terminal for liquids, not a gas offtake; the diameter is 8-10 inches, small for gas transmission but normal for a products line; and the stated purpose is export of a fuel, where Iraq's dry gas is consumed domestically in power stations. The Ministry's own 2013 inventory (the recovered JCCP deck) separately lists Iraq's product pipelines as 'shaiba - doura 10 inch' and 'shaiba - karkh 14 inch' -- i.e. Shuaiba is the origin of Iraq's PRODUCT pipeline system, which is where this row starts.

SAME CLASS AS THE LIBYA PASS: three condensate lines misfiled in GGIT (docs/country_notes/libya.md). Recommend a tracker-wide screen for GGIT rows whose only source describes a liquid -- Arabic-sourced rows especially, where 'زيت الغاز' and 'الغاز' are one word apart.

concerns.recommendation: WITHDRAWN -- do NOT act on this record. Superseded by the qc leg's P4067 classification record: keep P4067 in GGIT as gas, and refer the separate NEW crude line (Ahdab -> Zubaidiya PS, 16 in, 76 km, completed early 2024) to GOIT as a discovery candidate.
concerns.researcher_notes: RETRACTED 2026-07-28 and kept only as provenance. This record concluded that P4067 is a crude-oil line misfiled in GGIT, reasoning from Al-Ahdab being a CRUDE-OIL FIELD (the same conclusion docs/country_notes/iraq.md carried from the 2026-07-07 harvest). The inference is invalid: an oil field produces associated gas, and this line's destination is a POWER STATION ('Al-Zubaydia PWR St') -- a gas line from an oil field to a power plant is the most ordinary object in Iraq's gas network (Majnoon, Gharraf, Faiha, West Qurna and Buzergan rows are all that shape). Reading BOTH ASB2017 tables side by side settles it: OPEC lists the corridor's gas line in Table 9.9 ('Al-Ahdeb/Al-Zubaydia PWR St, OPC, 73, 16' = this row) and its crude lines separately in Table 6.9 ('Ahdeb/Wassit P P (2), OPC, 42, 45, 16, 10'), so it distinguished them deliberately -- the opposite of a misfiling. See the qc leg's record for the full ruling and notes/escalation-2026-07-28-iraq-gasoil-misfiled.md for the general rule this violated: key on what the source says the pipe CARRIES, never on what its origin field produces. ORIGINAL TEXT of this record, preserved verbatim for provenance: The pipe physically EXISTS (not a phantom), but GEM's Fuel=Gas classification is not supported by any independent source and appears wrong. GEM's own cited sources are all about the Al-Ahdab OIL field (BBC Arabic 2011 on Ahdab oil production start; Iraq Business News Ahdab field page; OPEC ASB 2017 p.134) — none describes a GAS pipeline. Independent sources uniformly describe the Al-Ahdab -> Zubaidiya feeder as a CRUDE OIL pipeline: (1) Al-Sharq (Iraqi press quoting the State Company for Oil Projects/SCOP) calls the project 'مشروع مد أنبوب النفط الخام المغذي لمحطة كهرباء الزبيدية – الأحدب' (the crude-oil feeder pipeline for Zubaidiya power station), completed at 76 km, delivered via two crude-oil pumping stations at Al-Ahdab and a receiving station at Zubaidiya. (2) MEES (2023) states Zubaidiya is an 'oil-fired power plant' supplied with crude oil (e.g. 24,000 b/d from Gharaf), not gas. (3) China.org.cn (Arabic, CNPC BRI feature) says the Al-Ahdab project 'يوفر الوقود لمحطة كهرباء الزبيدية' (supplies fuel to Zubaidiya, Iraq's largest power plant). The Al-Ahdab field's associated gas is processed to LPG for domestic distribution in Wasit, not piped as fuel gas to the plant. Endpoints (Al-Ahdab field -> Al-Zubaydia, Wasit), owner (Iraq Ministry of Oil), and FuelSource=Al-Ahdab all fit a crude line. Conclusion: real pipe, but it is a crude-oil power-station feeder mislabeled as a gas transmission trunk. Tier high: >=2 independent origins (SCOP/Iraqi press, MEES, China.org.cn) agree it is crude-oil / an oil-fired plant.

concerns.recommendation: Reclassify: this is NOT a natural-gas pipeline. It is a GASOIL (diesel) products EXPORT pipeline (Shuaiba pump station -> Khor Al-Zubair oil port). Fuel='Gas' is a mistranslation of the Arabic 'زيت الغاز' (zayt al-ghaz = gas oil / gasoil / diesel). Remove from GGIT (gas tracker) and move to GOIT as an oil/refined-products line, or flag as out-of-scope for GGIT.
concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: the pipeline is REAL and operating. Physically exists as a 46 km, 8-10 inch line from Shuaiba pump station (محطة ضخ الشعيبة, next to the Basra/Shuaiba refinery) to Khor Al-Zubair oil port; the Oil Pipelines Company (OPC) announced completion of its rehabilitation on 19 July 2024. Not a phantom. CLASSIFICATION (the finding): the row's OWN sole citation — al-mirbad (the OPC press announcement) — is titled and worded as 'أنبوب تصدير زيت الغاز (شعيبة - ميناء خور الزبير)' = 'GAS OIL / GASOIL (diesel) export pipeline (Shuaiba - Khor Al-Zubair Port)'. Body: 'أنجاز أعمال تأهيل أنبوب زيت الغاز (8 - 10) عقدة الممتد من محطة ضخ الشعيبة إلى ميناء خور الزبير النفطية ... بمسافة 46 كم ... زيادة الطاقة التصديرية لوقود زيت الغاز عبر المنفذ الجنوبي' = rehabilitation of the 8-10 inch GASOIL pipeline from Shuaiba pump station to Khor Al-Zubair OIL port, 46 km, to increase GASOIL FUEL export capacity via the southern outlet. 'زيت الغاز' is Arabic for gasoil/diesel — a refined liquid petroleum product, NOT natural gas ('غاز طبيعي'). Operator is the OIL Pipelines Company (شركة خطوط الأنابيب النفطية / OPC), GM Ali Abdul-Karim al-Mousawi. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: S&P Global Commodity Insights (15 Aug 2024, 'Iraq's ambition to become refinery powerhouse moves closer to fruition') independently reports Iraq 'completed the upgrade of a gasoil pipeline from the Shuaiba projects depot next to the Basrah refinery to the southern port of Khor Al-Zubair to resume exports of gasoil ... first exports of the product since 2003, completed in July [2024]' — a fully independent English trade source describing the same line as a GASOIL line (S&P is paywalled and returns 403 to url_verifier, so it is not in proposed_refs, but it is a genuine second independent source). Separately, Arabic port-context sources confirm Khor Al-Zubair port exports 'زيت الغاز' gasoil 'containing 500 ppm sulfur' by tanker — a refined liquid product with a sulfur spec, definitively diesel, not gas. ORIGIN OF THE ERROR: Iraqi News Agency's English rendering also mistranslated 'زيت الغاز' as 'gas' ('Gas export pipeline from Shuaiba to Khor Al Zubair Port has been successfully rehabilitated'), which is almost certainly how the 'gas' misclassification entered GEM. DUPLICATE: not a GEM-internal duplicate of any Iraq gas roster row (P1850/P2234/P7435 also touch Khor Al-Zubair but are different lines); not in the GulfPub crude list either. It is a cross-commodity misclassification (gas<-products), not a within-tracker duplicate. SPECS (all confirmed by al-mirbad, but for a gasoil line): length 46 km CONFIRMED; diameter 8 and 10 inch CONFIRMED (sheet '10,8' in); endpoints Shuaiba -> Khor Al-Zubair port CONFIRMED; province Basrah CONFIRMED; status operating CONFIRMED (rehab completed, exports resuming). PipelineType 'transmission' (trunk export line, not gathering) is fine as a type but it transmits gasoil, not gas.

concerns.recommendation: Fix endpoint direction/labels: Start = Akkas (Okaz) gas field, End = Akkas (Akaz) gas power station (Al-Qaim district, Anbar). concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — CONFIRMED (high). This is a real, operating dry-gas line. CLASSIFICATION — CONFIRMED. It is a dedicated gas-transmission line from field to power station (Al-Jibawi labels its type 'Dry gas'); not an oil/NGL line (no match to any GulfPub Iraq crude line), not gathering/plant-internal. DUPLICATE — NONE on the roster. Distinct from the separate, larger, NOT-yet-built Akkas→Anbar power station line (26″/26″/24″, three sections Akkas→T1→K3→Anbar power station near Hit) that Al-Jibawi lists as planned — do not conflate the two. concerns.researcher_notes: Three independent contradictions of 5,600 km. (1) Natural Gas World (11 Feb 2013), describing the same project with the same Asaluyeh->Damascus endpoints and the same 110 MMcm/d, gives 1,600 km. (2) GEM's own drawn route for this row measures LengthEstimateKm=1987.78 -- 2.8x shorter than the stated length, which no routing allowance explains. (3) Asaluyeh->Damascus is ~1,700 km great-circle, so 5,600 km would be ~3.3x the straight line. 5600 is Wikipedia's figure transcribed faithfully; 1,600 -> 5,600 is a plausible digit corruption somewhere upstream. Staged as a concern rather than a fill because the value is populated and published and a reference value is never auto-applied. Note the proposed 1,600 km rests on a single source and is itself below the drawn route, so it is a candidate, not a confirmed value.

concerns.recommendation: Re-check StartLocation. The only source says the gas source was undecided between West Qurna 2 (LUKOIL) and Rumaila (BP); GEM asserts Rumaila. Consider blanking to the governorate level (Basra) or noting both candidates in ResearcherNotes.
concerns.researcher_notes: Al-Ahram/Reuters (22 Nov 2017): it was not yet clear whether the gas would come from the LUKOIL-operated West Qurna 2 field or the BP-operated Rumaila field. StartLocation='Rumaila oilfield' therefore states as fact something the source explicitly leaves open. Low-stakes on its own, but it matters here because Rumaila is ALSO the origin of the genuine pre-1990 Iraq->Kuwait gas line (see the existence concern on this row), so an unsourced 'Rumaila' invites conflating the two.

concerns.recommendation: CAPACITY UNIT DEFECT: change CapacityUnits from 'MMSCMD' to 'MMcf/d', leaving Capacity=258. The source says 258 MMSCFD (cubic FEET). This corrects the computed CapacityBcm/y from 94.17 to ~2.67 -- a 35.3x error. Highest-priority item on this row.
concerns.researcher_notes: Proven from the row's own cited source, not inferred. The saymar.org SCOP deck states: '2.25 MMBOPD ultimate capacity of 56" Crude Oil pipeline (350 km) & 258 MMSCFD ultimate capacity of Sales and Fuel Gas 28" pipeline (350 km)'. MMSCFD = million standard cubic FEET per day. GEM recorded MMSCMD (cubic METRES), and 94.17 / 2.665 = 35.3, exactly the cf->m3 conversion factor -- arithmetic, not resemblance. Mechanical check on the PDF text: 'MMSCFD' appears 3 times, 'MMSCMD' 0 times. The deck's FEED section separately gives 284 MMSCFD, same unit. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE CELL: at 94.17 bcm/y this row is the SECOND-HIGHEST capacity in the entire GGIT tracker, behind only P4122 (Luxembourg, 104.34) and ahead of P0160 (Canadian Mainline, 71.18) -- on a 350 km 28-inch line. Nord Stream 1 moved 55 bcm/y on twin 48-inch. Physically impossible, and it distorts any Iraq or global capacity aggregate. SCOPE TESTED, NOT A CLASS: I screened all 63 MMSCMD rows with a parseable diameter against a generous diameter-based capacity ceiling. Only 4 exceed it by >2x, and P4041 is a lone extreme -- 14.2x, against 3.8x (P7697 Chile), 3.1x (P3297 India) and 3.0x (P7795 Brazil), all three of which are within the noise of a crude ceiling and may be legitimate. So this is one bad row, NOT a systematic MMSCMD ingest defect, and no cross-country sweep is warranted. One loose end worth a separate look: P4122 (Luxembourg, 104.34 bcm/y) fell out of the screen only because it has no parseable diameter, and 104 bcm/y for Luxembourg deserves its own check -- flagging, not claiming.

concerns.recommendation: ConstructionYear=2019 is contradicted by the row's own source, which shows the pipeline still at Concept Study level in Oct 2020. Blank it (or move 2019 to ProposalYear if that is where it belongs). Actual construction on the parent crude system began ~May 2026.
concerns.researcher_notes: Date-logic defect. The saymar.org SCOP deck (Oct 2020) states 'FEED Design was completed ... between North Rumailah (PS1A) to Haditha (PS5A) while the pipeline is at a Concept Study level', and gives project status as 'FEED & EISHA completed for Pump Stations, and Concept for the Pipeline'. A pipeline at concept stage in late 2020 did not begin construction in 2019. ProposalYear=2019 is a separate matter and is merely unsourced, not contradicted -- do not blank both on the same reasoning.

concerns.recommendation: Set StartYear1 2024 (was 2025). One cell. Status 'operating' stays, and the row's name, length (8 km) and diameter (24in) are all confirmed -- do not touch them.
concerns.researcher_notes:
This is ALL THAT SURVIVES of the status change this pass first staged against P6826 (see the status record, which retracts it). Al-Jibawi (June 2025): OPC 'completed in 2024 the construction of a 24-inch dry gas pipeline extending for 8 km from the Majnoon oil field ... to the NGL station in North Rumaila'. Completion in 2024 means StartYear1 = 2025 is one year late.

The 2025 was never sourced: the row's Start [ref] is a Facebook permalink that returns HTTP 400 and has no archive. So this is a dead ref carrying a wrong value -- the pattern this whole re-pass was built to find, and an argument for treating an unverifiable ref as a data-quality flag on the VALUE, not just a citation gap. Corroborating detail: al-Sharq (April 2024) has crews actively laying pipe, which is consistent with a 2024 finish and not with a 2025 one.

concerns.recommendation: Set StartYear1 2023 (was 1980). Separately, rename: this row is a 1,050 m SPUR off the Jambur-North Gas Company line feeding the Taza power station, not a 'Khormor-Jambur-Kirkuk' trunk. Both fixes are needed or the row keeps reading as a long 1980s trunk with an impossible length.
concerns.researcher_notes:
Two live sources agree and neither supports 1980 for this row. Al-Jibawi (2025): 'in November 2023, OPC completed the construction of a 16-inch dry gas pipeline that feeds Kirkuk power station in Taza. The pipeline extends from the Kormor fields with a length of 1,050 m. It bifurcates from the main pipeline, Jambur Station-North Gas Company, to feed Taza.' KirkukNow (2023-11-07) reports the same completion and adds, from a North Oil Company source, 'The pipeline extended between Khor Mor and Jambur WAS ORIGINALLY THERE, and a branch line was constructed in addition to rehabilitating the old pipe'.

So there are TWO pipelines here and GEM's single row conflates them: (a) a pre-existing Khor Mor-Jambur line, which is plausibly the 1980 asset and appears to have no GGIT row of its own, and (b) the 1,050 m branch built in 2023, which is what this row's length, diameter and capacity actually describe. Dating (b) to 1980 is the defect. The pre-existing trunk is a discovery/monitor lead.

This record also RETRACTS a suspicion from earlier in this pass: I flagged LengthKnown = 1.05 km as implausible for the row's name. The length is correct (1,050 m verbatim) and it was the name that misled -- logged because 'implausibly short length' is exactly the kind of flag a future pass would raise again.

concerns.recommendation: Set CapacityUnits 'bcm/y' -> 'MMcf/d'. Leave Capacity = 130 alone -- the number is right. This one-cell edit corrects the computed CapacityBcm/y from 130.00 to ~1.33.
concerns.researcher_notes:
SOURCE-PROVEN UNIT DEFECT, and the largest single overstatement in this pass (~98x). Shafaq News, 2021-02-18: 'The Iraqi Oil Projects Company completed the 22 km-130 CUBIC FEET natural gas pipeline supplying al-Qayyarah power plant', with 'a diameter of 18 inches'. 130 MMcf/d = 1.33 bcm/y. GEM tags the 130 as bcm/y.

THE MAGNITUDE IS THE ARGUMENT: at 130 bcm/y this 22 km, 18-inch spur to a single Iraqi power station is the SECOND-LARGEST-CAPACITY ROW IN ALL OF GGIT -- behind only the 10,200 km Transcontinental Gas Pipeline (171.70) and AHEAD of Texas Eastern (119.47), which is 14,202 km long. An 18-inch line cannot carry more than roughly 2-3 bcm/y at any realistic pressure. On a physical screen (ceiling ~= 0.0017 * D^2.5 bcm/y, calibrated so a 48-inch Nord Stream line reads 27.5) this row exceeds its ceiling by 55.6x -- the second-worst ratio among the 1,964 GGIT rows carrying both a capacity and a parseable diameter. See the memo for the honest framing of that screen: 72 rows exceed 2x and 13 exceed 4x, so 2x is a soft flag, not a defect finding.

THIS MAKES THE IRAQ CAPACITY-UNIT PROBLEM A CLASS, NOT A ONE-OFF. Three rows in one country now carry a correct number under a wrong unit label: P7477 (130 MMcf/d tagged bcm/y, ~98x HIGH), P4041 (258 MMSCFD tagged MMSCMD, ~35x HIGH) and P1841 (2.41 bcm/y tagged MMcf/d, ~120x LOW). Note the directions DIFFER, so this is not one systematic conversion applied wrongly -- it is careless unit tagging at ingest, which means it cannot be fixed by a blanket rule and has to be screened row by row. Two of the three put their row in GGIT's global top ten by capacity, so the defect is not cosmetic: it distorts any country or global capacity total. The screen also surfaces a WORSE non-Iraq row -- P2009 Mountaineer (US), 4,750 MMcf/d on an 8-inch, 5.5 km line, 157x its ceiling -- so this is very likely a tracker-wide class, not an Iraq one. Memo: notes/escalation-2026-07-28-iraq-capacity-units.md

concerns.recommendation: Do not trust Capacity=2.41 MMcf/d or Length=431 km without an independent source. Both are unverified and physically doubtful; leave flagged rather than green.
concerns.researcher_notes: Capacity 2.41 MMcf/d is physically implausible for a 431 km, 16-inch trunk line feeding a fertilizer/ammonia complex — a 16" line moves on the order of ~100+ MMcf/d, and an Al-Qa'im-scale ammonia plant would need tens of MMcf/d, not ~2.4. This tiny value is part of a suspicious cluster of sub-3 MMcf/d 'capacities' across the Iraq gas operating roster (P1845 2.00, P1846 0.67, P1847 0.70, P1848 2.10, P2231 0.89) that look like a systematic data artifact rather than real throughput. Length 431 km is also unverified and looks overstated: Baiji (≈34.93N,43.49E) → Haditha/K3 (≈34.07N,42.38E) → Al-Qa'im (≈34.37N,41.12E) is only ~250–260 km along a routed corridor, so 431 km is ~1.7x the plausible routed distance. No independent source AGREES with the GEM capacity, length, or 16" diameter — they are uncorroborated. Not silently passing.

concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED as a real line, but only via a single origin. The whole Iraq gas-operating roster (P1841/P1842/P4068/etc.) is transcribed from OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members' table (ASB 2016 Table 8.9 p.113-114; ASB 2017 Table 9.9). That table lists, under Iraq gas: 'Baiji/Al-Mashriq | OPC | 131 | 18' (columns are Connection from/to | Owner or operator | Length in MILES | Diameter in inches). Two editions (2016 & 2017) carry the identical row, so it is reproducible and authoritative, but it is one origin (OPEC), not two independent origins -> tier medium. No independent (non-OPEC, non-GEM) source I could find names this specific internal Baiji gas line. THE SHEET'S OWN SOURCES DON'T SUPPORT IT: (a) the wiki's ONLY outbound citation is 'OPEC ASB 2012 p.75', and that exact URL (opec.org/.../publications/ASB2012.pdf) now returns OPEC's HTML site shell, not the PDF (dead link, fails url_verifier). (b) The URUK / Jafar Dhia Jafar PDF cited on Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Diameter does NOT mention Baiji, Al-Mashriq/Mushraq, 211, or an 18in/160 line anywhere in its text layer (verified via pdftotext of all 8 pages) -- it only discusses North/South gas balance, Taji-Duara, and the Eastern 48in/350 line. The worklist's 'expected content present' pass on Capacity was a false positive ('160' is a substring of '16000 MW'). So that ref is irrelevant to this row and should be replaced. SPEC: Length 211 km = 131 miles x 1.609 -> OPEC's 131 mi rounds to 211 km, so GEM's 211 km is the CORRECT conversion (same miles->km pattern verified on sibling P1841: OPEC 'Baiji/Al-Qaiem 268 mi' = 431 km = GEM). Diameter 18 in = OPEC 18 in. CONFIRMED. Capacity 160 MMcf/d is UNSUPPORTED: OPEC's table has no capacity column and no other source states it; leave as-is but flag. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk -- it sits in OPEC's natural-gas pipelines table, operator OPC; not an oil/NGL line, not gathering. No concern. DUPLICATE: none. It is distinct from the separate OPEC row 'Mishraq cross road/Mousil PWR St | OPC | 38 mi | 12 in' (= GEM P4068) and from 'Baiji/Al-Qaiem' (= P1841). GEM's spelling 'Al Mushraq' conflates it with the Mishraq sulphur area near Mosul; OPEC's name is 'Al-Mashriq' (distinct token). ATTRIBUTION: OPEC gives owner/operator = OPC (Oil Pipelines Company), a Ministry of Oil subsidiary; GEM's Owner1 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' is defensible at the parent level but the specific operator is OPC. FuelSource 'Bajii' is a typo for Baiji and is consistent with the Baiji origin. Start province Saladin (Salah ad-Din) is correct (Baiji is in Salah ad-Din). END endpoint 'Al-Mashriq'/Mosul could not be independently geolocated (see routes).

concerns.recommendation: Treat the length (72 km), diameter (16 in) and capacity (0.70 bcm/y) as unverified single-origin figures; do NOT green any spec [ref]. concerns.researcher_notes: The sheet carries NO [ref] on any field (Status, Fuel, Capacity, Length, Diameter, Location, Owner all MISSING_REF). The only outbound citation on the gem.wiki page (wiki_citations.json) is OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, p.75 — an aggregate country-level statistical bulletin (reserves/production/exports) that does NOT enumerate individual Iraqi gas pipelines and cannot support a named 'Strategic-Hilla' line or any of its 72 km / 16 in / 0.70 bcm/y figures. I found no independent source that names a 'Strategic-Hilla' (or 'Strategy-Hilla') gas pipeline or corroborates any of its specs. What IS independently corroborated: (a) the Hilla gas-fired power station exists (Babil province, ~250 MW, natural gas, grid-connected 2012 — power-technology.com, worldpowerplants.com, coords 32.5422N/44.3213E); and (b) Iraq's central dry-gas grid reaches Hilla and feeds its power station (rawabetcenter.com 'History of natural gas in Iraq' lists power stations at Nasiriyah, Harth, Khor Al-Zubair, Najaf and Hilla on the network; attaqa.net describes 3 dry-gas networks ~3000 km). So a gas feed to Hilla physically exists and the 'gas' + 'operating' classification is sound — but the pipeline as characterized (its name and all four specs) is single-origin/unverified. FuelSource=Gas and Status=operating are the only fields I can defend from independent evidence.

concerns.recommendation: Review Status: reclassify 'operating' -> 'construction' unless physical gas flow through the 20-in line is independently confirmed. The Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas-investment (processing) project this line feeds is still under construction as of Dec 2025 with first operations expected Q1 2027.
concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and independently corroborated (2+ independent). (1) Ahmed A. Al-Jibawi, 'Shedding Light on Recent Oil & Gas Pipeline Projects in Iraq' (iraqieconomists.net, 2025 PDF): 'In 2023, SCOP completed a 20-inch dry gas pipeline extending from the Gharaf oil field in Dhi Qar Governorate to the 42-inch national dry gas pipeline for 76 km.' (2) al-Mirbad (2 May 2024, Arabic): describes the South Gas Company (شركة غاز الجنوب) Nasiriyah+Gharraf gas project fed by two raw-gas pipelines, the first '20-inch (عشرين عقدة) from the Gharraf field with capacity 120 MMcf/d (مقمق)' and a second 14-inch/80 MMcf/d line from the Nasiriyah field. Not a phantom, not a duplicate of any roster row (no other Gharraf/Rifai/Nasiriyah-field gas feed line; P1851/P1852 are Rumaila/Trans-Iraq->Nasiriyah, distinct). CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission — Jibawi says it ties the field into the 42-in NATIONAL dry gas trunk; Fuel=Gas correct; not an oil/NGL line (none of the GulfPub crude roster matches). SPEC CHECK vs GEM: Diameter 20-in CONFIRMED by BOTH al-Mirbad and Jibawi (high). Length 76 km CONFIRMED by Jibawi (medium; al-Mirbad does not state a length). Capacity 120 MMcf/d CONFIRMED by al-Mirbad (matches the ~130 MMcf/d Gharraf-field contribution cited in aggregate reporting). Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' defensible — built by SCOP (State Company for Oil Projects) and operated under South Gas Company, both Ministry of Oil entities (could be refined to 'South Gas Company'). THE CONCERN — STATUS: GEM says 'operating' (updated 2025-07-18) but the sheet's own cited al-Mirbad source (May 2024) describes the project at 'advanced stages — equipment installation and mechanical works, connecting equipment and internal pipe networks', i.e. UNDER CONSTRUCTION, and does NOT support 'operating' (the worklist ref-check already flagged al-Mirbad lacked 'operating'). Independent Egypt Oil & Gas (23 Dec 2025) states the Nasiriyah & Gharraf gas project (200 MMscf/d, South Gas Company + Baker Hughes) is 'under development' with initial operations 'expected in Q1 2027'. This 20-in/120-MMcf/d line is the RAW FEED line into that not-yet-operating processing complex per al-Mirbad. There is a genuine source conflict: Jibawi says the 76-km pipe itself was completed in 2023 (so the pipe may physically exist and could evacuate field gas), but two independent sources indicate the system it serves is not operating until 2027. Net: 'operating' is not clearly supported; flag for status review, do not silently pass.

concerns.pipeline_name: Khor Al-Zubair-Shatt Al Arab Gas Pipeline
concerns.recommendation: Change Status operating -> construction (mechanically complete but idle); blank/flag StartYear2=2025 until gas actually flows. Re-check after the Khor Al-Zubair FSRU commissions (target 1 June 2026).
concerns.researcher_notes: STATUS IS WRONG. The physical pipe is real and correctly described: 40 km, 42 in, from Khor Al-Zubair port to the Nazim Shatt al-Arab regulator, built by the Oil Ministry via Oil Projects Company (SCOP) + South Gas Company. Construction began 9 Feb 2025 and finished on schedule in June 2025 - but every source describes it only as 'ready to receive gas' (جاهز لاستلام الغاز), NOT as flowing/operating. Its sole purpose is to carry IMPORTED dry gas (regasified 'Gulf gas' LNG) from the planned Khor Al-Zubair floating LNG platform (FSRU). That FSRU does not exist yet: Iraq only signed the definitive FSRU deal with Excelerate Energy on 28 Oct 2025 (Hull 3407, still under construction in South Korea, commercial ops expected 2026), and the Ministry of Electricity set 1 June 2026 as the deadline to have the platform delivering 500 MMscf/d. So on the sheet's update date (2025-07-15) the pipe was mechanically complete but had NO gas source and could not have been 'operating.' The row's own Status refs corroborate this: the Facebook video and Baghdad Today link were tagged as failing verification because neither says 'operating' - they are groundbreaking/announcement clips, not a commissioning report. This is a completed-but-not-commissioned line; 'operating' overstates it. StartYear2=2025 (operations start) is likewise premature.

concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: The destination facility is strongly, independently real. Al Najibiya power station (محطة كهرباء النجيبية) is a ~500 MW gas/dual-fuel plant in the Al-Najibiya district of Basra city (west bank of the Shatt al-Arab), commissioned Jan 2016, owned by Iraq's Ministry of Electricity, 4x GE 9E gas turbines (power-technology.com profile; INA/ninanews Key=913132 on unit-5 maintenance). The pipeline itself is an OPC (Oil Pipelines Company / شركة خطوط الانابيب النفطية) dry-gas feeder rehabilitation. HOWEVER both citations the sheet uses trace to ONE origin: (a) opc.oil.gov.iq/?article=184 and (b) OPC's own Facebook post (facebook.com/PipelinesIQ) — that is a single institutional source, NOT two independent sources per the 2+ rule. Neither is currently content-verifiable: the OPC site now serves a bot-challenge/secure-gateway redirect (url_verifier gets 200 but the article body tokens النجيبية/الغاز are absent), and the Facebook URL 200s to a login/generic wall (token النجيبية absent). I could NOT find any independent third-party media (Iraqi press, INA, al-Mirbad, alkhaleej, attaqa, powernews) that names this specific Najibiya feeder line — searches surfaced only ANALOGOUS OPC dry-gas feeder projects (Najaf & Kirkuk cement plants, Kirkuk/Qayyarah power-station gas lines) and a separate 40 km/42-inch Khor Al-Zubair→Shatt al-Arab dry-gas trunk to Basra power stations (powernews.cc p=238204 — that is P7435, NOT this line). So the feeder is PLAUSIBLE and consistent with a documented OPC program of supplying Basra power stations with dry gas, but its independent corroboration is effectively zero. CLASSIFICATION: correctly gas (dry gas / الغاز الجاف), correctly NOT one of the GulfPub Iraq crude/NGL lines (none of them serve Najibiya PS). Mild caveat: at 4.5 km / 12 in this is a short dedicated power-station feeder/lateral rather than a trunk — GEM convention files dedicated power-plant gas supply lines as transmission, so 'transmission' is defensible but borderline. DUPLICATE: no other Najibiya row in the 36-line Iraq gas operating roster; not a relabel of any sibling. P7435 (Khor Al-Zubair–Shatt Al Arab, 40 km/42) is the likely upstream trunk that feeds this area, a distinct asset, not a duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: Operator 'Oil Pipelines Co' and Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' are consistent (OPC is a Ministry-of-Oil company and the Facebook page is literally OPC); province Basra and endpoint 'Al Najibiya power station' are correct. SPEC: length 4.5 km, diameter 12 in — single-origin OPC, unverifiable at present, so LOW confidence, not overturned (no conflicting figure found). Capacity blank and left blank (no sourced value).

concerns.recommendation: Correct Capacity/CapacityUnits. 130 bcm/y is impossible; the source's '130' is almost certainly ~130 mmcf/d (~1.34 bcm/y). Re-source the flow figure before re-stating; do not keep 130 bcm/y.
concerns.researcher_notes: CAPACITY IS WRONG. GEM records Capacity=130.00 bcm/y. The sole cited source (Shafaq / Ministry of Oil) states the line is '22 km-130 cubic feet' — a garbled unit, not a real bcm/y figure. 130 bcm/y is physically absurd: it is roughly the ENTIRE annual gas throughput of Iraq's national system and cannot pass through a 22 km / 18-inch spur feeding a single ~750 MW power station. A 750 MW gas plant consumes on the order of ~120-140 million cubic feet per day, so the source '130' most plausibly means ~130 mmcf/d (~1.34 bcm/y) — a ~100x units error in the GEM cell. I did not find an independent source stating the flow in explicit units (the academic paper gives plant MW, not gas volume), so I am NOT proposing a corrected number to auto-apply — flagging it for human correction of the units/magnitude. As-entered value is not defensible.

status_changes.researcher_notes: Verdict: keep 'cancelled', but ShelvedCancelledType must change from 'confirmed' to 'Presumed'. There was never a formal cancellation -- Wikipedia says so explicitly, and Syria's electricity minister stated in 2021 that the project had NOT been abandoned, a decade after the 2011 tripartite MoU. What ended it was political: Assad's fall in Dec 2024 removed the Iran-Syria basis for the corridor, and from Aug 2025 Syria began importing Azerbaijani (Shah Deniz) gas via Turkiye instead -- a different corridor serving the same demand. 'confirmed' asserts a cancellation event that no source records, which is the specific error here; the pipeline is dead by inference, and the row should say so. Also note the Status [ref] is an article about a crude OIL pipeline and does not belong on this cell (see that unit). The two refs recorded here are supporting analyses of the project's collapse, not a cancellation citation -- a 'stale' inference carries no ref by design.

Verdict: keep 'cancelled' but declare it an inference. The only cited source (Al-Ahram/Reuters, 22 Nov 2017) reports Iraq SELECTING Toyo Engineering to build the line -- initiation, not cancellation -- and records that no FID had been taken and talks had stalled on price. No cancellation was ever announced, in English or Arabic. What is independently documented is that the project's rationale lapsed: the gas was intended to help settle Iraq's 1990-invasion reparations, and the UNCC confirmed the final payment on 13 Jan 2022 ($52.4bn; ~1.5M successful claims of 2.7M filed), funded throughout by a levy on Iraqi OIL sales rather than gas in kind (UN News + Rudaw, both verified and independent of each other). With ~9 years of silence since the only project news, the 4y->cancelled rung is satisfied comfortably -- but by silence plus a lapsed rationale, not by an announcement. Hence ShelvedCancelledType='Presumed'. Deliberately NOT staging a CancelledYear: no source dates a cancellation and inventing one would be fabrication. Per the staged-JSON contract a 'stale' inference carries no ref, so the two reparations URLs are recorded here as supporting context for the reviewer, not as a citation for the Status cell.

Verdict UNCLEAR -- 'shelved' is contradicted, but I cannot responsibly name the replacement. This row is the 28-inch sales/fuel gas leg of the Basra(North Rumaila)-Haditha corridor, and its own cited source (SCOP deck, Oct 2020) describes 2 PARALLEL pipelines in ONE existing corridor under one EPCF scope: 56-inch crude + 28-inch gas. The 56-inch crude twin is tracked in GOIT as P0544 'Basra-Aqaba Oil Pipeline' with Status='construction' -- so the two legs of one trenched project currently read 'construction' and 'shelved' in GEM's two trackers. And the crude leg really is moving: PM directive 26 Apr 2026, $1.5bn approved under the Iraqi-Chinese agreement, work started ~1 May 2026, 56-inch pipe manufacturing under way (The National, Shafaq, Hydrocarbon Processing, AGBI -- four independent, all verified). WHY NOT PROPOSE A CHANGE: every one of those 2026 reports describes the CRUDE line only. None mentions sales gas, fuel gas, a 28-inch line, or any gas infrastructure -- I checked Shafaq's scope reporting specifically for this. So the gas leg's presence in the executed scope rests on the 2020 EPCF scope document plus a third-party project listing, which is not enough to flip a status. Route to Update: confirm with SCOP/Ministry of Oil whether the 28-inch gas line is in the 2026 award. If yes -> 'construction'; if the crude line was carved out alone -> 'proposed' or 'shelved' with a current source. Either way 'shelved' as it stands is unsupported. Note this row also carries a proven capacity-unit defect and a contradicted ConstructionYear -- see __VALIDITY__.

No contradiction with GEM values.

'Okaz' = عكاز = Akkas gas field in Al-Anbar province, western Iraq; the pipeline connects the field to the (still-under-construction) Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant. GEM Status = 'proposed' is well corroborated: the pipeline is not yet built. Per the July 22 2025 Schlumberger/Midland Oil field-development contract, a PARALLEL contract (with SCOP, the State Company for Oil Projects) is to be signed to build a pipeline network linking wells to central processing units, with gas then directed to the Anbar power plant. The National: 'Additional contracts will be signed to build surface installations and lay pipelines connecting the wells to central processing units' (verified). Iraqi News: names the SCOP pipeline-network contract and the 100 mmscfd/Anbar power-plant destination (verified, contains Akkas+Anbar+SCOP). Xinhua: confirms the newly-signed deal to develop the field with output routed to the Anbar power plant (verified). Field currently produces only ~40 mmscfd; the transmission pipeline is planned/to-be-built = proposed. Caveat on independence: all three outlets report the same July 2025 Ministry-of-Oil announcement, but each carries distinct detail (The National's 'long-awaited'/pipeline-to-CPU line vs Iraqi News's SCOP-network specifics), and none cite GEM. Tier high on the value (proposed/planned pipeline). The original current_ref (iraqieconomists.net PDF, Al-Jibawi) returns HTTP 200 but the url_verifier could not extract the 'Okaz'/'Anbar' tokens from it (appears to be a scanned/non-text-extractable PDF), so it is not staged; the three fresh news sources supersede it.

Unit was DEAD_LINK: the only citation (iraqieconomists.net Al-Jibawi PDF) is live (HTTP 200) but on WebFetch its text does NOT mention Akkas/Okaz, Anbar pipelines, or a T1-K3 segment at all — it is a misattributed citation, so it cannot support the Status. Kept as ok=false/contains_value=false. GEM entity = a PROPOSED 3-segment gas trunk from the Okaz (Akkas) field via stations T1 and K3 to Al-Anbar (T1-K3 = 26in, owner Iraqi Ministry of Oil); this is the wider gas-TRANSPORT network, distinct from the short ~30km line that already feeds the adjacent Akkas power station. Corroborated 'proposed' with two independent professional outlets: (1) The National (2025-07-22) — 'Additional contracts will be signed to build surface installations and lay pipelines connecting the wells to central processing units,' gas then directed to the Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant (still under construction) = pipeline network planned, not built, owner Iraqi Ministry of Oil. (2) MEES (2025-07-25) — states current output (~40mn cfd) runs via an existing 30km line to the Akkas power plant, while SCOP will ADD new flow lines from SLB-drilled wells to new processing units under a forthcoming contract = the expanded transport pipelines are planned. Both distinguish the built local feed from the still-to-be-built transport network, matching Status=proposed. Tier high: two reputable independent outlets each with their own operational reporting; caveat — both cover the same July 2025 SLB/Akkas award, though the qualitative 'planned pipeline network' status is also consistent with earlier (2022) MEES and Iraq Oil Report coverage. iraq-businessnews.com/2025/07/22 aggregator returned HTTP 401 (not usable).

'Okaz' = the Akkas/Akaz gas field (عكاس/عكاز) in western Al-Anbar; GEM segment 'K3-Al-Anbar' is the dry-gas transmission line delivering Akkas-field gas to the ~1,640 MW Al-Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant (Ministry of Oil, 24 in). RE-CHECK of the dead-link current_ref (iraqieconomists.net Al-Jibawi PDF): the file is live (HTTP 200) but its extracted text contains no mention of Okaz/Akkas or this pipeline, so it does NOT corroborate the value — dropped. FOUND corroboration for the 'proposed' status: attaqa.net (Al-Taqa, 2025-10-04) and mustaqbl.net both report, in near-identical wording, that 'the Council of Ministers recently referred/approved for execution the project to construct the fuel pipeline transporting from the Akkas gas field to the [Anbar] plant site' (مجلس الوزراء أحال/وافق مؤخراً مشروع إنشاء أنبوب الوقود الناقل من حقل عكاس الغازي إلى موقع المحطة للتنفيذ) — i.e. the transmission line is at the cabinet-authorization / pre-construction stage while the plant itself is ~95% complete and awaiting Akkas field development. routes.corridor_desc: Inferred corridor (NOT from a route source): from Baiji (Saladin) southwest to the Haditha/K3 pump-station area on the Euphrates, then northwest up the Euphrates valley through Anbar to the Al-Qa'im fertilizer complex near the town of Al-Qa'im on the Syrian border. Endpoints are named and defensible (Baiji and Haditha are well-known towns; the Al-Qa'im complex coordinate 34°22'N 41°07'E is from FAS → ~34.37N,41.12E). The 'K3' waypoint follows the pipeline name and the oil-corridor station convention, not an independent gas-route source, so the actual alignment is unknown and the bound is loose. Routed length ~250–260 km vs the sheet's 431 km — do not treat the corridor as authoritative.

new_rows.name: Akkas-Syria Gas Pipeline
new_rows.monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold leg (c) concrete step (and arguably (a) sponsor). The Akkas-to-Syria/AGP gas EXPORT pipeline has no MOU, tender, FEED, EPC award, permit, or FID of its own — it exists only as a long-standing aspiration (2004 Egypt/Jordan/Syria/Lebanon framework to connect AGP to Iraq's grid; ~2009 Akkas–Europe-via-Türkiye concept) that stalled in the Syrian war / ISIS's 2014 seizure of Akkas, and is now only under 'renewed discussion' post-Assad. All concrete 2025-26 activity attaches to the Akkas FIELD (SLB drilling Jan 2026; Midland Oil Company lead; earlier Ukrzemresurs/KOGAS-Daewoo contracts), whose gas is targeted at domestic power generation, not a cross-border export line.
new_rows.researcher_notes: Match-to-existing re-checked and ruled out: distinct from P0450 (Iran–Iraq–Syria/'Friendship', Iranian gas Asaluyeh→Damascus, cancelled), P1841 (Baiji-K3-Al Kaem, terminates at Al-Qa'im INSIDE Iraq, operating), and P7460/P7466/P7467 (Okaz–Al-Anbar, domestic Okaz-field feed to Anbar power plant, proposed). No existing GEM gas row captures an Akkas→Syria→AGP cross-border export link. However it does not clear the Discovery add-threshold. Add-threshold assessment: (a) sponsor — NOT identified for the pipeline itself (SLB/Midland Oil Company/Ukrzemresurs/KOGAS are Akkas FIELD operators, not pipeline sponsors); (b) endpoints — roughly present (Akkas, al-Anbar, ~30 km S of Al-Qa'im on the Syrian border → Syria → Arab Gas Pipeline toward Türkiye/Europe); (c) concrete step — ABSENT: no MOU/tender/FEED/EPC/permit/FID for the export pipeline. Sources: karamshaar.com AGP/Syria analysis (Jan 2026, explicitly frames Akkas→AGP as historical/aspirational, halted by war, only under renewed post-Assad discussion) and en.wikipedia Arab_Gas_Pipeline (2004 four-country framework to link AGP with Iraq's grid) — both URL-verified (200 + expected substring). Corroborated independently by Energy Intelligence and OilPrice coverage of the Akkas field (domestic-supply focus; SLB drilling started Jan 2026). Note the recent concrete Iraq–Syria cross-border activity is a different project and a different commodity: the Kirkuk–Baniyas OIL pipeline revival (oil, not gas). Confidence: findings well-supported by 2+ independent English sources, but the pipeline itself remains rumor/aspiration — low tier as an early-stage monitor item. Recommend keeping on the watchlist; revisit if a cross-border gas MOU/tender/EPC or a formal Iraq–Syria gas-transit agreement is signed.

new_rows.name: Al-Faw Grand Port LNG-Abu Ghraib Supply Pipeline
new_rows.monitor_reason: Add-threshold leg (b) fails: endpoints/route indeterminate. The '130 km connecting pipeline' has contradictory, physically impossible endpoints across sources ('130 km pipeline from Al-Faw port' per emilecon vs '130km at Abu Ghraib' per PM readout/MEED/Goalfore) — Al-Faw port to Abu Ghraib is ~550 km, so a 130 km line cannot connect them, making the route unstageable. Corroboration also fails the 2+ independent test: all figures trace to one 26 Aug 2025 cabinet press readout (PM media office) reprinted by English trade press.
new_rows.researcher_notes:
SKEPTICAL VERDICT: monitor, not new_row. Match-to-existing re-checked against all 54 Iraq gas rows in discovery_context.json — no existing row is this LNG-import connecting pipeline (P7435 Khor Al-Zubair FSRU tie-in is a separate completed 40 km/42in line; P7434 Mahmudiyah-Besmaya is a distinct grid segment; P5857 Zubair-Faw is a shelved 18in/105km line in the opposite delivery direction; the 45 km Mahmudiyah-Abu Ghraib PS line reported completed June 2025 is a grid feeder, not this LNG trunk). Confirmed the consolidator's finding that no roster line runs north from Al-Faw port.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED: Iraq's Cabinet approved a >10,000 MW power package on 26 Aug 2025 (per PM media office) that bundles LNG reception infrastructure at Al-Faw Grand Port — jetty + FSRU + 'connecting pipelines: 17 km at Al-Faw and 130 km at Abu Ghraib' — feeding 3,000 MW CCGT plants at Al-Faw (developer Superior Technology Systems, UAE) and Abu Ghraib (developer Emirate Technology Company), each ~400 MMscf/d imported LNG, 25-yr BOO, GE Vernova technology. The FSRU itself was later awarded to Excelerate Energy (~$450M). Concrete step (leg c) IS met (cabinet approval).

WHY IT FAILS AS A STAGEABLE ROW: (1) Corroboration — verified both English evidence URLs (url_verifier OK, 200 + content), but MEED/Goalfore/Emilecon all reprint the SAME 26 Aug 2025 cabinet readout; not 2+ independent sources. In-country Arabic reporting closest to primary (attaqa.net, 16 Aug 2025) does NOT mention any 130 km line — it describes different, already-completed pipelines (40 km Khor Al-Zubair-Shatt Al-Arab by South Gas Co./Petroproject = existing P7435; 45 km Mahmudiyah-Abu Ghraib PS by Petroproject) and reports the FSRU still at the bid stage (6 firms invited, 2 qualified, pending Diwani Order Committee). (2) Endpoints/route — the '130 km' figure is internally contradictory (emilecon: 'from Al-Faw port'; PM/MEED: 'at Abu Ghraib') and physically impossible for an Al-Faw->Abu Ghraib connection (~550 km apart), so no coherent route or endpoints can be established; the consolidator's 'port-to-national-grid trunk' reading is unsourced inference. (3) No distinct pipeline sponsor — the connecting pipelines are an unattributed bundled component of the LNG import/IPP package, not a separately identified project.

RECOMMENDATION: Monitor. Re-check when the FSRU/import scheme reaches FEED/EPC award for the connecting pipeline specifically, or when a source gives a coherent, corroborated route (from/to + length). Confidence tier low; single reprinted primary source.

new_rows.name: Chemchemal-Bazian Gas Pipeline

values.RouteNotes: Announced as a dedicated 40 km line from the Chemchemal field to industrial consumers in the Bazian area; no published GIS route. To be built by (unnamed) private-sector companies.

new_rows.researcher_notes:
NEW ROW. Passes all three add-threshold legs: (a) sponsor = Pearl Petroleum consortium (Dana Gas + Crescent Petroleum operating) developing the Chemchemal field under a KRG concession; (b) country + endpoints = Iraq, Chemchemal field (Sulaymaniyah) -> Bazian industrial area; (c) concrete step = 10-year Gas Sales Agreements signed Jan 2026 with Bazian-area offtakers (Mass/Bazian/Delta/Gasin/Sulaimani Cement), $160m committed to field development, first gas targeted H2 2027. Corroborated by >=2 independent sources: Crescent Petroleum press release (operator/primary), World Oil (independent trade press), OilPrice analysis, and Iraqi News all confirm a 'dedicated 40 km pipeline' from Chemchemal to Bazian industrial consumers, privately funded, deliveries from H2 2027. All four URLs passed url_verifier (200 + expected content). Confidence: HIGH on existence, endpoints, 40 km length, sponsor, and the Jan-2026 GSA milestone.

MATCH CHECK: Distinct from existing GEM rows. P6823 (Khormor-Pirdawood PP) and P4047 (Khormor-Erbil, construction) are Khor Mor-sourced lines feeding power plants / Erbil; this is a Chemchemal-field-sourced, privately built line to Bazian INDUSTRIAL (cement) consumers. No roster row originates at Chemchemal. Not a duplicate.

DELIBERATE OMISSIONS (skeptical calls): (1) Capacity LEFT BLANK. The widely cited '142 MMscf/d' is the FIELD-WIDE GSA offtake total across ALL new industrial customers (both the Bazian cement cluster AND the separate Erbil line to Van Steel), per World Oil ('up to 142 MMscf/d collectively across all industrial customers'). Assigning the full 142 MMscf/d to the Bazian line alone would overstate it; sources do not disaggregate a per-line rating. (2) Owner LEFT BLANK. Sources say the pipeline is 'to be built by private-sector companies' but name no specific builder/owner entity; did not run/stage a new owner entity. (3) $160m cost NOT attributed to the pipeline — it covers three wells + an extended well test facility + enabling infrastructure for the whole field program, not the pipeline specifically. (4) FIDStatus blank — GSAs are offtake agreements, not a pipeline construction FID. (5) No published GIS route -> RouteAccuracy 'no route'. Sibling candidate 'chemchemal-erbil-industrial-gas' is a separate build (Van Steel offtaker) and is vetted separately.

new_rows.name: Chemchemal-Erbil industrial gas supply pipeline
new_rows.monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold legs (a) and (b). (a) No identified sponsor: the only wording anywhere is 'new pipelines are to be built by private-sector companies' -- the companies are unnamed; Pearl Petroleum (Dana Gas/Crescent) is the gas seller under the GSA, not stated as the pipeline builder. (b) Endpoints not established: the delivery point is Van Steel Company in Erbil governorate, but no source gives an origin, route, length, or diameter -- 'Chemchemal-Erbil' is an inferred name, and it is equally plausible the Erbil supply arrives as a tie-in/spur off the existing Khor Mor-Erbil corridor (GEM P4047, 36-in, construction) rather than a standalone Chemchemal-Erbil trunk. (c) is only partially met: the 10-year GSA with Van Steel (signed Jan 2026, first gas H2 2027) is a concrete commercial step for the gas supply, but there is no tender, FEED, or EPC award for the pipeline itself. Contrast: the sibling Bazian line IS specified (dedicated 40 km, Chemchemal field direct to Bazian) in the same release, showing the sponsors describe pipelines concretely when they exist as defined projects -- the Erbil leg deliberately is not.
new_rows.researcher_notes: Vetted 2026-07-04 (CB). Sole primary source is the 26 Jan 2026 Dana Gas/Crescent Petroleum (Pearl Petroleum) press release announcing 142 MMscf/d of 10-year GSAs from the Chemchemal field, with first gas H2 2027; Van Steel Company (Erbil governorate) is the sole Erbil offtaker named. On the pipeline serving Erbil the release says only that 'new pipelines are to be built by private-sector companies to supply gas to industrial users in Erbil and Bazian' -- no builder, origin, route, length, diameter, cost, or schedule. All other coverage checked (World Oil, Iraqi News, Egypt Oil & Gas, Sharjah24, MEES, Rudaw) reprints the same release; zero independent corroboration of a distinct Erbil pipeline project, so tier = low / independent = false. Match-to-existing re-checked against the 54-row Iraq gas roster: not the same project as P4047 Khormor-Erbil Gas Pipeline (that is the Khor Mor-to-Erbil power corridor, already under construction pre-dating this GSA) and not P4053 Erbil-Duhok; but a tie-in delivering Chemchemal gas to Van Steel via the P4047 corridor cannot be ruled out -- if that materializes, the correct treatment is likely a note/spur on P4047, not a new row. Re-vet when a builder is named, an origin/route is disclosed, or a pipeline tender/EPC award appears (watch Dana Gas/Crescent releases and KRG MNR through 2026-2027 ahead of H2 2027 first gas). The two cited URLs passed scripts/url_verifier.py on 2026-07-04 (the rudaw.net/business/26012026-amp URL was dropped -- it 200s to a nav shell without the article text and failed verification). The concrete sibling (dedicated 40 km Chemchemal-Bazian line) is handled under its own candidate slug.

new_rows.name: Diyala Gas Fields Supply Pipeline (Gilabat-Qumar / Khashim Ahmer-Injana)
new_rows.monitor_reason: Fails add-threshold leg (c) as applied to a pipeline, and (b) is only partial. The concrete steps on record (20-year development contracts signed Feb 2023 and activated Oct-Dec 2023; 3D seismic phase 1 completed Apr 2025) are FIELD-development milestones, not a pipeline-specific step (no pipeline tender / FEED / EPC / route / FID). No distinct transmission pipeline is defined anywhere: the primary source commits only to generic 'pipelines and infrastructure to supply gas' to 'nearby power plants' with no route, length, diameter, or named endpoints, so it cannot be confirmed to be a distinct transmission line rather than field/plant-boundary supply infrastructure. Project is still in appraisal (seismic), and the 'first gas within 18 months' (mid-2024) target has slipped past April 2025.
new_rows.researcher_notes: SPONSOR (leg a) MET: Crescent Petroleum (UAE; Crescent won these blocks in the 2018 5th licensing round, contracts re-signed/activated 2023). ENDPOINTS (leg b) PARTIAL: source = Gilabat-Qumar and Khashim Ahmer-Injana gas fields, Diyala Province; destination = 'nearby power plants' -- trade press (Petroleum Economist, 2024) names Mansuriyah power plant, ramping 120 -> up to 520 MMscfd feeding Mansuriyah plus other nearby Diyala stations. No pipeline route/length/diameter is published. VOLUMES are field production (initially 250 MMscfd, up to ~520 MMscfd), NOT a verified single-pipeline throughput. CONCRETE STEP (leg c) is field-level only. MATCH-TO-EXISTING re-checked against all 54 Iraq gas rows: no existing row covers a Crescent new-build from these Diyala fields. P4058 'Eastern Iraq Gas Pipeline' (operating, cap 350) is the pre-existing Iranian import corridor into Diyala/Baghdad, NOT this build -- not a match. CONFIDENCE: medium. Corroboration: Crescent primary PR (2023-02) + Argus (independent, 2023-02) + Crescent seismic PR (2025-04); Zawya is a reprint of the Crescent PR and does not count as independent. All four cited URLs verified HTTP 200 via url_verifier.py. RECOMMENDATION: monitor for a pipeline-specific milestone (defined route/endpoints, pipeline EPC/tender, or FID) before staging a new_row; re-check on the next annual pass given the field development is active.

new_rows.researcher_notes: NEW ROW. Confirmed distinct from the two existing Halfaya-area gas rows: P6832 (Bazargan-Halfaya, 18in, INBOUND sour gas from the Iran-border Buzurgan complex into Halfaya) and P4058 (Eastern Iraq Gas Pipeline, 48in / 350 capacity) — neither matches this 24in / 21km OUTBOUND dry-gas outlet, and endpoints/diameter rule out corridor overlap with P4058. Add-threshold met on all three legs: (a) sponsor = PetroChina Halfaya operating consortium (field operator; built by China Petroleum Pipeline Company / CPECC, a CNPC subsidiary); (b) endpoints = Halfaya oil field -> Al-Kahla power station, Maysan governorate; (c) concrete step = operating (commissioned early 2013). EXISTENCE + STATUS = high confidence (independent: Iraq Oil Report 2013 EN, Zawya 2023 EN, Al Jazeera 2024 AR, NS Energy/TotalEnergies for the operator consortium). SPEC (24in diameter, 21km length, 40 MMcf/d initial pilot flow) rests primarily on the Iraq Oil Report Feb-2013 report, a reputable specialist source, but is effectively single-sourced for the exact figures -> overall tier MEDIUM. Capacity left BLANK: the only figure available is the 40 MMcf/d 2013 pilot flow, which is a throughput at start-up, not a stated design capacity, and is now outdated (the 300 MMscf/d Halfaya GPP came online 2023-2024). Owner/Parent reflect the Halfaya field service-contract consortium (PetroChina Halfaya 37.5% operator; TotalEnergies 18.75%; Petronas Carigali 18.75%; Missan Oil Company 25%) per NS Energy / TotalEnergies; note the asset is legally state-owned under Iraq's technical service contract, and Missan Oil Company operates the processing complexes (Arabic sources, June 2026). EndLocation set to Al-Kahla power station (the documented terminus of this 24in line); the Halfaya GPP's dry gas also feeds the Amara and Maysan power plants (Zawya/Al Jazeera 2023-2024), but that later delivery may run on additional/separate lines and is NOT conflated into this row's spec. mubasher.info Arabic article on the Kahla gas-connection line opening exists but repeatedly timed out in url_verifier, so it was NOT cited. No fabricated URLs; all cited URLs passed url_verifier. Route: no official GIS geometry located; not staged (geometry -> routes repo).

values.OtherEnglishNames: Iraq-Jordan Gas Pipeline; Basra-Aqaba twin pipeline (gas component); Rumaila-Aqaba gas pipeline

new_rows.researcher_notes: MATCH CHECK: No Jordan-touching or Basra-Aqaba gas row exists in the 54-row Iraq gas roster (nearest are P7573 Basra-Ceyhan, to Turkey, and P0450 Iran-Iraq-Syria) so this is not an existing GEM gas row. CONFIRMED DATA: parallel gas line rated 350 MMcf/d within Iraq and 258 MMcf/d on the Jordanian stretch (258 used as Capacity value); twin-corridor length 1,680 km (~1,044 mi) — the gas line runs parallel to the oil line in the same corridor, so LengthKnown reflects the shared corridor length (no separate gas-only geometry published). CONFIDENCE: high — >=2 independent English outlets (UPI 2013, Pipeline Technology Journal, MEED, Rudaw 2018, Bayan Center 2020) agree on sponsors, endpoints, 258 MMcf/d gas, and 1,680 km, and are not reprints of one wire. Recommend ShelvedCancelledType handled at apply time (confirmed cancellation, not presumed).

new_rows.name: Miran gas field export pipeline (to Bazian power plant)
new_rows.monitor_reason: Add-threshold leg (c) fails for the PIPELINE: no pipeline-specific concrete step exists (no MOU, FEED, EPC award, tender, permit, or FID for any Miran-Bazian line). The only firm commitment is the May 2025 binding term sheet + PSC for the FIELD (Miran Energy JV = HKN Energy + ONEX Group with the KRG), and the field itself is still in an 18-20 month exploration/appraisal phase (50-70 MMcf/d initial). Leg (b) is also weak: the pipeline endpoints have never been stated as a pipeline project - the line is inferred from MEES (Aug 2025) saying gas from the fast-tracked 100 MMcf/d processing plant 'will feed the nearby Bazian power plant', plus a Miran Energy recruitment posting listing a 'sour gas trunk line and sweet gas delivery line and connection to the Bazian Power Plant' as engineering scope. Neither is a project milestone, and it is not even confirmed a standalone evacuation pipeline of material length is required. Sponsor (leg a) is clear, but one leg alone = monitor, not new_row.
new_rows.researcher_notes: Match-to-existing re-checked independently against all 54 Iraq gas rows in discovery_context.json: no Miran- or Bazian-destination pipeline exists (nearest Kurdistan gas lines P6823 Khormor-Pirdawood, P4047 Khormor-Erbil, P7457 Semel-Duhok are distinct) - not matched_existing. Field-level facts corroborated by multiple independent outlets and confirmed high-tier: MEES 15 Aug 2025 (Miran partners fast-tracking a 100 MMcf/d gas processing plant, first gas targeted 2H 2027, gas to feed the nearby Bazian power plant); Kurdistan24 19 May 2025 (HKN Energy + ONEX Group launch Miran Energy JV, binding term sheet with KRG for phased development of the ~8 tcf Miran field, Sulaymaniyah gov., domestic-supply focus, PSC expected shortly); OilPrice (18-20 month exploration/assessment, 50-70 MMcf/d projected). All four cited URLs re-verified this session via scripts/url_verifier.py (kurdistan24 contains 'Miran Energy'; MEES, OilPrice, and the iqjscout recruitment posting each contain 'Bazian'). CONFLATION GUARD: the widely reported dedicated ~40 km Chemchemal-to-Bazian-industrial-area pipeline is a SEPARATE candidate (vetted under slug chemchemal-bazian-gas), and a completed 16 km / 20-inch line to Bazian PP is a Khor Mor / Qaiwan Group project (orient-pipeline.com) - neither is the Miran line; they must not be used to manufacture Miran endpoints, length, or diameter. No source (English or in-country coverage through 2026) states a Miran-Bazian pipeline route, length, diameter, capacity, or pipeline contract - all pipeline specifics are inferred, so no values are staged. entity_lookup (gas): Miran Energy, HKN Energy, and ONEX Group are all new entities (fuzzy hits were false positives) - stage on promotion. Confidence: field-level facts high/independent; the pipeline itself low/inferred -> MONITOR. Re-check triggers: Miran PSC signature followed by a pipeline FEED/EPC/tender or permit, or a confirmed standalone Miran->Bazian evacuation line with stated endpoints/specs. Excluded URLs (failed verification this session): onexholding.com post (HTTP 404); iraq-businessnews.com JV story (HTTP 401).
